features: TOUCHES THE DATABASE: ELEVEN MIGRATIONS — All re-runnable and all in the test that restarts them halfway, which now snapshots indexes as well. Accrual period on invoices (competenza_dal/al); the competenze_capitolo table (the accrual stretches of a budget item, such as the heating season); the subentri table (registered ownership changes) and its details (title document, lease end and regime, appurtenances as child rows); saldi.subentro_id (the settlement pair); an index on the unit–person periods; the frozen time data on righe_riparto (period, step, days); removal of tipologie_spese, always empty; piani_rate.esercizio_id with backfill; already-paid contributions keyed per unit and person, plus the settlement-cancellation columns; on righe_riparto the holding stretch each row covers (titolarita_dal/al), not just how many days. Nothing to do when upgrading: existing plans stay identical and say so.

DATES ENTER THE ALLOCATION — On ordinary expenses the share of a unit that changes hands is split by days between who leaves and who enters, over the accrual period: the one declared on the item (one or more stretches), else the management period, else the fiscal year. On extraordinary expenses one day counts, the assembly resolution date (art. 63 disp. att. c.c.; Cass. 24654/2010, 24236/2025): whoever held the unit that day pays it all. The resolution date is asked when the plan is created, with no default; without it the engine stops and asks. For urgent works the accrual is declared on the invoices. The frozen detail carries period, step and days; allocation printouts show them (“245 days”).

IF THE ACCRUAL CHANGES THE RECIPIENTS, GENERATION STOPS AND SHOWS IT — Who enters, who leaves, for how many days out of how many; you proceed with a checkbox and a note, frozen in the plan. Someone leaving without a successor: the uncovered days go to the next link of the cascade for those days (a vacant unit charges the owner), not spread over those who were there; an owner leaving without a successor leaves an uncovered part, with its reason, and generation asks for a justification.

“REGISTER A CHANGE OF OWNERSHIP” — Sale or donation, lease start and end, creation and termination of a usufruct, from the unit's holders list. One date: the leaver's period closes the day before, the entrant's opens, the history stays whole. The “What will change” panel, computed server-side: records, issued instalments and proposed settlement, who remains liable (art. 63 par. 4 and 5), what does not change. Checkbox and note when issued instalments or a recipient are affected. Appurtenances follow, the title PDF goes to the unit's documents, the certified copy can be recorded later from the history, an optional lease-expiry reminder. “Who has held this unit” history. A row with history is not deleted, the person is not replaced, the role of a row in a registered change is not edited; a unit with registered changes is not deleted.

SETTLEMENT OF ALREADY ISSUED INSTALMENTS — Issued instalments are not touched: the change writes two balance rows summing to zero, a credit to the leaver and a debit to the entrant for the days-based share (on extraordinary expenses, all on one side per the resolution). Purple lock, never edited one at a time, absorbed by the next plan. Computed to the cent like the panel: row by row, each on the holding stretch it actually covers; item by item when an item has its own accrual, net of amounts already paid split like the engine does, including the drafts of a plan that has already posted to the journal (that plan is no longer recalculated). Handles chains of changes within the same year and usufruct termination with several bare owners. Waiver with a note; cancellation from the history until a plan absorbs it.

REFUNDING A CREDIT — From the statement of someone with available credit (a seller, an overpayer): cash account, date, amount up to the credit. A “refund to owner” entry (RMB protocol), counter-entry by origin, reversible; the available credit updates in print too; the “Credits to offset” widget gets the second exit “Statement · refund”. Fixed a defect dating from 1.9.1: the movements list did not recognise adjustments and reversals (enum compared with a string).

ALREADY PAID CONTRIBUTIONS FOLLOW THE PERSON — A payment recorded with the person offsets only that person's share; without a person it belongs to the unit. Before, after a change of ownership, the leaver's payment offset the entrant.

ALSO CHANGED — A holding's start date counts as an effective date only with a predecessor (a row of the same pair closed the day before, or entry through a registered change), otherwise it is a census date and the row is “open since forever”. “Today” is the user's, not the server's. An issued instalment does not go back to draft if a change registered after issue has settled it. Changing the resolution date on a generated extraordinary plan warns to recalculate, and issuing with stale shares is refused. With “Urgency” approval does not ask for a resolution. The inherited cash deficit no longer counts the settlement pair as funding. Diagnostic commands kondomanager:verifica-delibere and verifica-titolarita. «Manage overrun» from the dashboard opens the plan with the overrun item already selected and the overrun amount (before, only the management arrived, and the notice spoke of an invoice cart that ordinary plans do not have); the «Item accrual» card lists only the chapters with something left to fund, and with many items you can search by name. On a top-up plan the «Item accrual» card proposes the accrual already declared for that item in the parent plan («as in plan …») instead of the management period: before, heating declared on the season fell back to the whole year in the overrun plan. When recording an invoice, the accrual that item has in the plan is shown under the item, with the rule: ordinary allocation follows those days, not the accrual declared on the invoice. An invoice line still at zero is no longer an «over budget» on a chapter already beyond its estimate: the warning lights up once there is an amount. On a prior-year invoice the accrual panel asks for the period in which the cost accrued: if the part not covered by the opening balances ends up in an extraordinary plan, without that date the current year's resolution allocates it — and after a handover the incoming owner would pay for a cost from when the unit belonged to the outgoing one.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO — Succession is not a type of change (recorded as a sale with “succession of…” details; the proper type comes in the next version). A sale with reserved usufruct has no path of its own: the form refuses it and says how to record it by hand. Drafts of a plan already posted stay with the leaver and are settled, not reassigned to the entrant. “Nobody's” days are measured where no holder of the role is in force. Reversals inflate the statement totals, as always.

DOCUMENTATION — Fourteen new decisions in the ownership-change project (11–24), the inherited-opening rule rewritten; in-app guides “Register a change”, “Instalment plan”, “Plan detail”, “Balances” with cards on pro rata, gate and pair; texts saying “dates do not enter the calculation” rewritten. Four independent verifications with their fixes in the internal documents.
